page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a high-capacity storage-oriented virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization, it provides 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 48.0 GB of RAM. A defining characteristic of this instance is its massive integrated local storage capacity of 35,433 GB backed by magnetic HDD drives, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

In synthetic benchmarks, single-threaded CPU speed trends toward the lower quartile, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 911.0 and a single-core stress-ng rating in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core CPU metrics scale moderately well, posting an average Passmark CPU score of 10,074.03 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 37.67 GB/sec. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 54.9 GB/sec, though Passmark memory scoring places general memory responsiveness in the lower 25th percentile. Static web serving throughput reaches 5.49 GB/sec, while Redis SET performance remains steady at 8.27 million operations per second.

The trade-off between lower per-core compute performance and high magnetic storage density makes this instance cost-efficient for heavy data-retention requirements where raw single-threaded execution is secondary. Provisioning massive local HDD capacity alongside 12 vCPUs eliminates the need for separate network-attached bulk storage volumes for high-volume logging and batch processing. The ecs.d1.3xlarge is well suited for big data storage nodes, archive aggregation, log analysis clusters, and bulk ETL workloads requiring large local disk footprints.
